Senses.Note: Dahui answers a question about the higher matter with a warning not to tell dreams before a fool. Tian’an uses the same line when pressed to identify the mind settled by Bodhidharma. Shiyu says it after challenging a possible objection to his sermon. Guxue offers it to a monk who asks what lies beyond guest and host, and Juelang answers with it when asked where a person stands after space dissolves. In each exchange the proverb blocks a premature story in place of seeing what the question demands.

Shixi Xinyue first puts ancient and present speakers, successful and unsuccessful sayings, together as a business with nothing to grasp. He then gives the elephant-and-lion pair, strikes the Chan seat, and says that he almost could not get it on its feet. The large animal images belong to this sequence of speaking and striking: the passage supplies a present gesture rather than leaving the pair as an impressive description. Chushi Fanqi uses the pair in a praise of Manjusri. He has described Manjusri carrying a thousand bowls, appearing with five topknots, teaching princes, and guiding monks.
